title: Evaluating Compositional Generalization in Transformers: The Role of Composition Equivalence and Module Coverage
abstract: arXiv:2611.13498v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Compositional generalization is an important form of out-of-distribution generalization, defined as the ability to train on some combinations of modules (e.g., functions such as sort, filter) and then generalize to unseen combinations. Despite substantial empirical work evaluating compositional generalization in transformers, findings have been inconsistent because evaluations were often conducted on a limited set of train-test splits, defined in an ad hoc manner. Through a systematic evaluation, we identify two key aspects of the train-test distribution that strongly affect performance: composition equivalence and module coverage. We show that the apparent performance of direct models (trained only on final outputs) results primarily from exploiting composition equivalences, meaning different sequences of modules that reduce to identical end-to-end functions. translated_title: 评估Transformer中的组合泛化：组合等价性与模块覆盖度的作用
translated_abstract: 组合泛化是一种重要的分布外泛化形式，其定义为：在若干模块组合（例如 sort、filter 等函数）上进行训练后，能够泛化到未见过的组合的能力。尽管已有大量实证工作评估了 transformer 的组合泛化能力，但由于评估往往只在有限的、以临时方式定义的训练-测试划分上进行，研究结果并不一致。通过系统性评估，我们识别出训练-测试分布中强烈影响性能的两个关键方面：组合等价性和模块覆盖度。我们表明，直接模型（仅在最终输出上训练）所展现的性能主要源于对组合等价性的利用，即不同的模块序列可以归约为相同的端到端函数。当基准测试消除这些等价性时，模型性能会显著下降。
tldr: 本文通过系统性评估发现，训练-测试分布中的组合等价性与模块覆盖度是决定 transformer 组合泛化性能的两个关键因素，直接模型的优异表现主要来自对组合等价性的利用，一旦消除这些等价性，性能将显著下降。
en_tdlr: Through systematic evaluation, this paper identifies composition equivalence and module coverage as two key aspects of train-test distributions that strongly affect compositional generalization in transformers, showing that the apparent performance of direct models mainly stems from exploiting composition equivalences and drops significantly when such equivalences are eliminated.
